ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of $1.2\mathrm{T}$, directed from south to north. A proton enters the magnetic field in a vertically downward direction, and the force exerted by the magnetic field on the proton is $9.6\times10^{-14}\mathrm{N}$. The proton carries a positive charge of $1.6\times10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$.

1. What is the speed of the proton when it is injected?
2. In which direction does a proton deflect in a magnetic field?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of $1.2\mathrm{T}$, directed from south to north. A proton enters the magnetic field in a vertically downward direction, and the force exerted by the magnetic field on the proton is $9.6\times10^{-14}\mathrm{N}$. The proton carries a positive charge of $1.6\times10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$. 1. What is the speed of the proton when it is injected? 2. In which direction does a proton deflect in a magnetic field?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a cross-shaped direction marker, with the top marked "North", the bottom marked "South", the left side marked "West", and the right side marked "East", so north can be regarded as upward and east as rightward. Then reason: The problem gives the magnetic induction intensity B=1.2 T, with direction from south to north; the proton charge q=1.6×10^-19 C; the magnetic field force F=9.6×10^-14 N. The proton velocity is vertically downward, perpendicular to the magnetic field direction from south to north, so F=qvB, obtaining v=F/(qB)=9.6×10^-14/(1.6×10^-19×1.2)=5×10^5 m/s. When judging the deflection direction, take east as +x, north as +y, and vertically upward as +z, then the proton velocity v is in the -z direction, and the magnetic field B is in the +y direction. The proton is positively charged, and the force direction is v×B=(-z)×(+y)=+x, that is, it deflects eastward.
